issue_context.title: BUG: Unsafe decimal parse for arrow types silently truncates value instead of raising an error
issue_context.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.


### Reproducible Example

```python
>>> ser = pd.Series(["1.2345"], dtype=pd.ArrowDtype(pa.string()))
>>> ser.astype(pd.ArrowDtype(pa.decimal128(1, 0)))
0    1
dtype: decimal128(1, 0)[pyarrow]
>>>
```


### Issue Description

The value is silently truncated, instead of raising an error that the decimal cannot be safely rescaled. This example would raise this error in pandas 2.1.4:

```
>>> ser = pd.Series(["1.2345"], dtype=pd.ArrowDtype(pa.string()))
>>> ser.astype(pd.ArrowDtype(pa.decimal128(1, 0)))
pyarrow.lib.ArrowInvalid: Rescaling Decimal128 value would cause data loss
>>> pd.__version__
'2.1.4'
>>>
```

For decimal most usages values accuracy, and silently truncating the value does not seem desirable, also if the original series was a decimal, then this error would be raised:

```
>>> ser = pd.Series(["1.2345"], dtype=pd.ArrowDtype(pa.decimal128(5, 4)))
>>> ser.astype(pd.ArrowDtype(pa.decimal128(1,0)))
pyarrow.lib.ArrowInvalid: Rescaling Decimal128 value would cause data loss
>>>
```

So it seems unusual when casting a decimal from a string, the value is silently truncated during rescale, but when casting it from another decimal, then there's no truncation during the rescale operation and an error is raised.



### Expected Behavior

```
>>> ser = pd.Series(["1.2345"], dtype=pd.ArrowDtype(pa.string()))
>>> ser.astype(pd.ArrowDtype(pa.decimal128(1, 0)))
pyarrow.lib.ArrowInvalid: Rescaling Decimal128 value would cause data loss
```

This was the behavior in pandas 2.1.4.

comments:
63999823379155ffa17af0ed5fbac25696010cb2 is the first bad commit
Author: Matthew Roeschke
Date:   Thu Dec 14 13:06:54 2023 -1000

    BUG: time strings cast to ArrowDtype with pa.time64 type (#56490)

cc @mroeschke

> For decimal most usages values accuracy, and silently truncating the value does not seem desirable
> ...
> but when casting it from another decimal, then there's no truncation during the rescale operation and an error is raised.

Agreed the inconsistency is not desirable, but with some dtypes we do perform lossy operations when the user requests it, e.g. 

    pd.Series([1.2345]).astype(int)

or from float64 to float32. It's not clear to me that we shouldn't allow this case to be lossy as well. I don't think it's surprising that `.astype(pd.ArrowDtype(pa.decimal128(1, 0)))` could be lossy, but as you point out perhaps special consideration should be given since Decimal types are specifically geared to avoid the issues of floating point data.

FWIW: The example of casting float to int fails with pyarrow types because it is lossy:

```
>>> a = pd.Series([1.2345], dtype="float64[pyarrow]")
>>> a.astype("int32[pyarrow]")
pyarrow.lib.ArrowInvalid: Float value 1.2345 was truncated converting to int32
>>>
```

Looks like numpy types allow the lossy conversion but pyarrow types not do not.
